title: [Activity] Running SVD and SVD++ on MovieLens

cues.en: That's definitely enough theory.
cues.zh: 理論絕對已經夠多了。

cues.en: Let's see SVD in action and recommend some movies with it.
cues.zh: 看看 SVD 實際運作，用它推薦一些電影。

cues.en: So, open up Spyder.
cues.zh: 開啟 Spyder。

cues.en: And close out any existing windows so we don't get confused.
cues.zh: 關閉現有視窗，避免混淆。

cues.en: A shortcut for that by the way is Control + Shift + W.
cues.zh: 順帶一提，快速鍵是 Ctrl+Shift+W。

cues.en: Open up everything inside the MatrixFactorization folder inside your course materials.
cues.zh: 開啟課程教材 MatrixFactorization 資料夾中的所有檔案。

cues.en: Let's start by looking at the SVDBakeOff.py file.
cues.zh: 先看 SVDBakeOff.py。

cues.en: Surpriselib includes a couple of different SVD implementations.
cues.zh: SurpriseLib 包含幾種不同的 SVD 實作。

cues.en: One is SVD more or less as we've described it, and the other is called SVD++.
cues.zh: 一種大致就是剛才描述的 SVD，另一種叫做 SVD++。

cues.en: It's a slight variant of SVD that ended up being part of the winning system for the Netflix Prize.
cues.zh: 它是 SVD 的小變形，最後成為 Netflix Prize 獲勝系統的一部分。

cues.en: The difference is fairly subtle.
cues.zh: 差異相當細微。

cues.en: It has to do with the actual loss function that is used while running stochastic gradient descent.
cues.zh: 與執行隨機梯度下降時，使用的實際損失函數有關。

cues.en: In SVD++, this loss function takes into account the idea that merely rating an item at all, is some sort of implicit interest in the item, no matter what the rating was.
cues.zh: 在 SVD++ 中，損失函數會考慮：只要對某個項目評分，不管評分是多少，本身都代表某種隱含興趣。

cues.en: But that was enough to make SVD good enough to win.
cues.zh: 但這點差異，就足以讓 SVD 好到獲勝。

cues.en: There's not much to talk about in the code itself.
cues.zh: 程式碼本身沒太多需要說明。

cues.en: The actual implementation of SVD and SVD++ is handled by the library.
cues.zh: SVD 與 SVD++ 的實作，由函式庫處理。

cues.en: You can look at SurpriseLib in GitHub if you want to see how the code works under the hood, but it's way too complex to walk through right now.
cues.zh: 如果想看內部程式碼如何運作，可以到 GitHub 查看 SurpriseLib，但它太複雜，現在不適合逐一講解。

cues.en: When you start dealing with algorithms as complex as SVD, it's almost never a good idea to write it from scratch yourself.
cues.zh: 開始處理 SVD 這種複雜演算法時，自己從零寫起，幾乎從來不是好主意。

cues.en: Use third party, open source libraries that have been used and validated by others instead.
cues.zh: 應該使用其他人已用過、驗證過的第三方開源函式庫。

cues.en: The odds are just too great that you'll mess up some tiny thing that ruins your results somehow.
cues.zh: 因為太容易在某個微小地方出錯，導致結果毀掉。

cues.en: So let's go ahead and kick this off, and see what sort of results we get.
cues.zh: 開始執行，看看得到什麼結果。

cues.en: It will take several minutes to run, so we're just going to pause and come back when it's done.
cues.zh: 需要幾分鐘，所以先暫停，完成後再回來。

cues.en: SVD++ in particular takes some time.
cues.zh: 尤其 SVD++ 需要一些時間。

cues.en: These accuracy results are the best we've seen so far, and as expected, SVD++ is a little bit better, actually getting below 0.9 RMSE.
cues.zh: 這些準確程度結果，是目前看過最好的；如預期，SVD++ 略好，RMSE 實際降到 0.9 以下。

cues.en: That's pretty impressive, as accuracy goes.
cues.zh: 就準確程度而言，相當厲害。

cues.en: But what do the actual top-N recommendations look like?
cues.zh: 但實際 Top-N 推薦長什麼樣子？

cues.en: Let's scroll down and take a look at SVD first.
cues.zh: 向下捲動，先看 SVD。

cues.en: Okay, these don't look too bad.
cues.zh: 好，看起來不差。

cues.en: Gladiator, Moon, Wallace and Gromit, those are all movies I enjoyed, and recall that I selected our test user as someone who has similar tastes to myself.
cues.zh: Gladiator、Moon、Wallace and Gromit 都是我喜歡的電影，記得，我選的測試使用者與自己品味相近。

cues.en: Many of the other results are movies that are literally on my list of movies I want to watch, so on the surface, it seems that the SVD recommender did a pretty good job of recommending a mix of movies I know about,
cues.zh: 許多其他結果，真的就在我的待看清單裡。因此表面上，SVD 推薦系統做得不錯，混合了我知道的電影，

cues.en: that give me trust in the system, and recommending somewhat more obscure titles that I'm genuinely likely to enjoy.
cues.zh: 讓我信任系統，也推薦一些較冷門、但我真的可能喜歡的片名。

cues.en: This seems like something worth testing on real people for sure.
cues.zh: 這確實值得拿真實使用者測試。

cues.en: The difference in accuracy with SVD++ was subtle, so I wouldn't expect to see any big changes in its results, but let's see.
cues.zh: SVD++ 準確程度的差異很小，所以預期結果不會大幅改變，但看看吧。

cues.en: Hm, well we do see a few of the same movies that SVD came up with, but we see a few new ones, too, like Harry Potter and Indiana Jones.
cues.zh: 嗯，有幾部與 SVD 相同，但也有 Harry Potter、Indiana Jones 等新片名。

cues.en: If user 85 really hasn't seen those movies yet, I'm kind of amazed that they haven't come up before.
cues.zh: 如果使用者 85 真的還沒看過，我有點驚訝它們之前都沒出現。

cues.en: So all things being equal, SVD++ seems like the one I'd experiment with first.
cues.zh: 因此，其他條件相同時，我會先實驗 SVD++。

cues.en: I like these results.
cues.zh: 我喜歡這些結果。

cues.en: It seems like something good is happening here.
cues.zh: 看起來確實發生了好事。

cues.en: That's the thing with algorithms that extract latent factors, they can be a little bit spooky in how well they distill users down to their fundamental interests, and how well they distill movies
cues.zh: 擷取潛在因子的演算法就是這樣，能夠如此精準地將使用者濃縮成根本興趣，將電影

cues.en: into what makes them unique.
cues.zh: 濃縮成獨特之處，有時讓人有點毛骨悚然。

cues.en: Matching the two up with SVD can be a powerful idea.
cues.zh: 用 SVD 把兩者配對，是很強大的想法。

cues.en: That was a lot of theory to wrap your head around, but we got a pretty good payoff for it here.
cues.zh: 雖然要理解很多理論，但這裡得到的回報相當不錯。
